Subject: Upcoming renewal — looking to expand & move to H100

Hi Hannah,

Our renewal is coming up (Dec 15). Weve been running on a reserved A100 pool and want to discuss adding capacity and moving a portion of the committed GPUs to H100s or L40S. Primary asks: 1) whats the delta in cost vs throughput; 2) how quickly can you provision a mixed pool; 3) can we get hard throughput guarantees for peak inference windows?

Were preparing an internal econ write-up and need a Redwood performance-per-dollar case and a proposed amendment to the committed pool. Carlos will handle procurement questions. Can you share a proposal and any SLA/term changes?

Thanks,
Elena

Elena — appreciate the heads up. High level answer up front: we can support a mixed pool (A100 + H100/L40S) under the same reserved contract with a term amendment; provisioning lead time for production-dedicated capacity is ~4-6 weeks depending on region and GPU mix. We can offer a throughput guarantee for a routed subset of traffic (canary + SLA attachment) and will propose an economic case showing expected perf/$ improvements.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood delivers a short perf-per-dollar analysis (Ben) and a recommended split (e.g., 40% H100, 60% A100 or full L40S pilot)
- Draft term amendment with monthly committed vCPU/GPU counts and an optional burst band (Dev)
- Joint ops review call next week to align provisioning schedule and acceptance tests

Ill attach an econ workbook and draft amendment for your review. If procurement needs a PO timeline, Carlos, what date do you need to sign by to keep Dec 15 start?

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt

Subject: Performance-per-dollar brief (A100 -> H100/L40S trade-up)

Elena, team — attaching a concise TCO/perf workbook. TL;DR summary below so you can paste into your internal memo:

Summary:
- H100 offers ~1.8-2.4x raw FP16 throughput for our typical 4k-context models vs A100, and L40S provides similar throughput to H100 on large-batch inference with better AVX efficiency for INT8 paths.
- Effective perf-per-dollar gains depend on utilization and batching: at 65% steady utilization with our continuous batching, moving 50% of reserved capacity to H100 yields ~30-40% lower cost per effective token served for low-latency high-concurrency workloads (50-200 RPS).
- For BrightAIs profile (70 tokens/resp, median latency target 120ms), recommended path: convert 30-50% of committed GPUs to H100s now, keep remainder as A100s for latency-sensitive tails, and run a 6-week L40S pilot on a routed subset to validate INT8 benefits.

Operational notes:
- Provisioning: 4 weeks for a mixed-pool rollout if quantities < 80 GPUs; 6+ weeks for larger orders or cross-region placement.
- SLA: we can define throughput targets by route with an SLO-based credit schedule; see attached SLA draft.
- Price delta example (per-GPU-month, illustrative): A100: $3,600 -> H100: $5,200 (net after trade-in credits depends on term). We included amortized uplift and estimated token-unit cost in the workbook.

Attachments: redwood-hw-tradeup-tco-v2.xlsx

Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Elena/Carlos/Hannah — attaching a draft amendment (amendment-draft-terms.pdf) and proposed throughput-guarantee-sla.docx. Key items called out:
- Committed capacity: add 40 additional reserved GPUs (configurable mix), term starts Dec 15, 12-month and 24-month pricing options included.
- Trade-up credit: one-time credit applied per returned A100 equivalent when upgrading; credit scales by remaining term. Example table included in the draft.
- Throughput SLA: per-route SLO with measurement window and credit multipliers. Credits expressed as percent-of-monthly-commit applied to next invoice; also include objective credit for missed tail-latency targets.
